reviews.title: Horrible!!!
reviews.text:
Google Maps has become incredibly frustrating to use, especially with Apple CarPlay.

Every single time I open Google Maps in my car, I get an unwanted pop-up telling me to navigate to Work or Home. I DON’T WANT TO GO TO WORK OR HOME! I rarely navigate to either location. I have turned off every notification for Google Maps and Apple Maps, disabled Siri suggestions, turned off app suggestions, cleared significant locations and routes, and changed every setting I can find. Yet this ridiculous pop-up STILL appears.

Why isn’t there a simple setting to TURN THIS OFF? I shouldn’t have to hit the X every single time I get in my car just to use a navigation app. Let users decide where they want to go instead of constantly pushing unwanted destinations at them.

And while we’re at it, the voice navigation needs serious work. The Google Maps voice is frustrating, unnatural, and nowhere near as pleasant or useful as the Siri voice. Give users the option to use Apple’s Siri voice for turn-by-turn directions! It’s ridiculous that we’re stuck with Google’s voice when Siri’s voice is already available and works seamlessly throughout the rest of the Apple ecosystem.

A navigation app should make driving easier, not make getting in your car an aggravating experience.

Please fix the CarPlay pop-ups, give users control over suggestions, and let us choose the Siri voice for navigation.

I’m tired of fighting with an app that is supposed to make my life easier.

reviews.title: Extremely Disappointing Work Progress and Disruption to Residents by Building Works - Contractors
reviews.text:
My experience with Building Works Ltd. at our condominium has been extremely disappointing.

The workers were on site for approximately two hours, yet for much of that time there appeared to be very little activity. Residents have been instructed to keep their balcony blinds closed and have effectively lost access to their balconies because of the ongoing renovation work.

What makes this particularly frustrating is the lack of visible progress. After approximately two months of this project, the actual work completed appears minimal. On this particular day, workers spent approximately 15 minutes per unit before leaving.

Residents deserve better than this. We understand that building renovations take time, but that does not justify poor productivity, unnecessary disruption, and the loss of use of our own balconies without meaningful progress.

A professional contractor should demonstrate proper planning, efficient use of working hours, respect for residents, and clear communication.

One unit can be completed from start to finish in a single day. Yet here we are, nearly three months into the project, and the work is still nowhere near halfway completed. This is simply unacceptable.

The question is simple: if residents are expected to tolerate this level of disruption, shouldn’t they at least see consistent and measurable progress?

Very disappointing experience.

We travelled from Canberra with our family specifically to have lunch at AMehdi Persian Restaurant, relying on the opening hours published on its website, which indicated that the restaurant was open for lunch on Monday.

Unfortunately, when we arrived, the restaurant was closed.

I even called the owner while standing outside the restaurant. He told me that it should be open, despite the fact that the doors were clearly closed and there was no service available.

This was an extremely frustrating and disappointing experience, particularly after travelling from another city and making plans with our family.

Restaurants have a responsibility to keep their advertised opening hours accurate and to communicate any changes clearly to customers. Providing incorrect information and leaving customers stranded outside is simply unacceptable.

Based on this experience, I cannot recommend AMehdi Persian Restaurant. I hope the management takes customer service and the accuracy of its advertised opening hours more seriously.

reviews.title: One reluctant star - airport transfer failed leaving my elderly mother and young daughter stranded.
reviews.text:
I booked a Beniconnect transfer from Jávea to Alicante Airport for my mother and 15-year-old daughter on 27 October 2026.

They were at their hotel from 5.45am for a 6am collection. They report that the bus drove past them and that my daughter actually tried to chase after it to attract the driver’s attention. They were not collected.

Four days earlier, I had specifically provided Beniconnect with both passengers’ telephone numbers, explaining that I would not be travelling. The company confirmed in writing that these numbers had been added to the booking.

However, Beniconnect called my UK number instead. The call disconnected as I answered, and my repeated attempts to call back went unanswered.

My mother and daughter had to arrange an emergency taxi costing €175 to reach the airport.

Despite numerous emails, Beniconnect’s Customer Service Manager has refused reimbursement, repeatedly arguing that the service was delivered because GPS tracking showed the vehicle attended the hotel.

The passengers were never transported.

I have now escalated the matter through formal consumer complaint and payment dispute procedures.

A deeply disappointing experience, particularly given that a teenager and her grandmother were relying on this transfer to catch their flight.

reviews.title: Horrible, Horrific and Just Plain Lousy
reviews.text:
Google Maps has repeatedly failed me while navigating Turin, Genoa, and Milan. Instead of making unfamiliar cities easier, it often added confusion with late instructions, abrupt rerouting, and walking directions that were difficult to follow.
In Turin, it struggled with the dense central street layout and one-way system, sometimes putting me in the wrong lane or directing me toward turns too late to take them safely. In Genoa, pedestrian routing was particularly frustrating around narrow streets and elevation changes; the suggested paths were unclear and did not always feel practical. In Milan, lane guidance and turn-by-turn timing near busy intersections were inconsistent, forcing me to slow down or stop to figure out where I was supposed to go.
The recurring issues were late voice prompts, confusing reroutes, and directions that seemed to prioritize a route on the map rather than a realistic, easy-to-follow path. For a navigation app, that is a fundamental failure. The map data and interface may look polished, but none of that matters if the app cannot reliably guide someone through a city.
After getting lost multiple times across three major Italian cities, I cannot recommend Google Maps for travel navigation. I expect clearer instructions, earlier warnings, better pedestrian routing, and more dependable rerouting before I would trust it again.

As you can’t be searching through or navigating the app while driving, it’s imperative that they create a version which allows you to choose road types at the onset of a journey. 

I got a serious fright when it made us end up on a logging track near Tahune, remote Tasmania, when we had been travelling from Hobart to Tahune. reviews.text:
This app used to be ok. Until last year, now it’s started mapping out the longest and busiest routes to go - and I mean it guides you TO a traffic jam and leads you around 10 minutes to an hour out of your way. My last trip should have only taken 20 minutes each way. Unfortunately the map guided me to a huge traffic jam, and the busiest roads - literally taking me INTO traffic that was bumper to bumper with people beeping horns and almost having accidents, and buses almost sideswiping me - when literally there was a road with no traffic on it straight ahead but it wanted me to turn into traffic that was stopped dead. It doesn’t show you that the roads are jammed. 
It doesn’t calculate the time given the traffic situation.

I do not recommend this app until it’s fixed.
